name: Via Ferrata Ivano Dibona
summary: A historic, panoramic high-altitude ridge route in the Cristallo group, featuring the famous 30-meter suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Tridentina (Brigata Tridentina)
summary: One of the most popular and scenic via ferrata routes in the Dolomites, ascending a vertical wall near the Sella Pass and ending with a suspension bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Sci club 18
summary: A highly demanding and athletic modern route directly under the Faloria cable car, offering steep, exposed, and strenuous vertical climbing.

name: Via Ferrata Punta Anna
summary: A steep and exposed classic ridge route climbing the prominent southern buttress of Tofana di Mezzo.

name: Via Ferrata Giuseppe Olivieri
summary: The demanding continuation of the Punta Anna route leading further up towards the summit of Tofana di Mezzo.

name: Via Ferrata Bolver-Lugli
summary: A long, vertical, and challenging high-alpine route on Cimone della Pala in the Pale di San Martino group.

name: Via Ferrata delle Bocchette Centrali
summary: A masterpiece of ledge systems in the Brenta Dolomites, offering world-class exposure along natural horizontal rock shelves.

name: Via Ferrata delle Bocchette Alte
summary: One of the highest and most strenuous routes in the Brenta Dolomites, traversing spectacular ladders and narrow ledges.

name: Via Ferrata Lagazuoi (Gallerie del Lagazuoi)
summary: A unique historic route passing through a continuous network of steep tunnels bored by Italian soldiers during WWI.

name: Via Ferrata Giovanni Lipella
summary: A massive, classic alpine route circling and ascending the Tofana di Rozes, passing through a WWI tunnel and open vertical faces.

name: Via Ferrata Oskar Schuster
summary: An alpine route leading up to the summit of Plattkofel (Sasso Piatto) in the Langkofel Group.

name: Via Ferrata delle Aquile
summary: An incredibly exposed and exciting modern sport route on Paganella, featuring dramatic aerial ladders and a bridge.

name: Via Ferrata Rino Pisetta
summary: One of the most physically demanding and difficult via ferratas in Italy, ascending a near-vertical limestone wall near Lake Toblino.

name: Via Ferrata Monte Albano (Ottorino Marangoni)
summary: A legendary, heavily overhanging athletic sport route located above the town of Mori near Lake Garda.

name: Via Ferrata Gerardo Sega
summary: A unique itinerary on the walls of the Adige Valley, traversing an enormous overhanging amphitheater on a spectacular natural shelf.

name: Via Ferrata Che Guevara
summary: A massive endurance route climbing over 1,200 meters of vertical elevation up the east face of Monte Casale.

name: Via Ferrata Col dei Bos
summary: A popular modern sport route near Cortina, ideal for intermediate climbers, featuring beautiful slabs and historical ruins at the base.

name: Via Ferrata Innerkofler-De Luca
summary: A classic historic route ascending the Paternkofel (Monte Paterno) right next to the iconic Tre Cime di Lavaredo.

name: Via Ferrata Giulio Segata
summary: A short but incredibly technical and strenuous vertical crack-and-chimney climb on Monte Bondone.

name: Via Ferrata Gamma 2
summary: An athletic and highly exposed vertical sport route scaling the limestone pillars of Monte Resegone near Lecco.

name: Via Ferrata Zandonella
summary: A steep and rugged alpine route scaling the south face of the Sexten Rotwand (Croda Rossa di Sesto).

name: Via Ferrata Constancia (Sass Rigais)
summary: A high alpine route climbing to the highest summit of the Geisler (Odle) group in the western Dolomites.

name: Via Ferrata dei Tre Signori
summary: An athletic route located in the Piedmont region (Lanzo Valleys), featuring multiple suspension bridges and steep rock plates.

name: Via Ferrata del Gabiola
summary: A sustained and airy route exploring the rocky spurs of the Maritime Alps in Liguria/Piedmont borderlands.

name: Via Ferrata Gamma 1
summary: A highly enjoyable, varied ladder-and-ridge progression ascending the lower cliffs of Monte Resegone.
